# FDG8032

> DO NOT use arrays for properties if the property would have to return a new array (e.g., a copy of an internal array) every time the property getter is called.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.3 Choosing Between Arrays and Collections.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1819
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Test profile: test classes are public only for the test framework; their signatures are not API. CA1819 reports every externally visible array property, whether or not the getter returns a new array; a property that returns its array directly is FDG8003's concern. Array properties of attribute classes are not reported (probe with SDK 10.0.402), so coverage is partial. Turning the property into a method or a collection property changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; CA1819 has no code fix. CA1819 is shared with FDG5025 and FDG8003.

## From the book

This ensures that users will not write the following inefficient code:

```csharp
//bad design
for(int index=0; index< customer.Orders.Length; index++) {
  Console.WriteLine(customer.Orders[i]);
}
```
